Kaufman's Adaptive Moving Average (KAMA) and the Efficiency Ratio — Trend vs Sideways

On this page

  1. 1. The problem it solves
  2. 2. The Efficiency Ratio (ER) — "how straight was the road?"
  3. 3. From ER to KAMA (Kaufman's default 10, 2, 30)

  5. 5. The important part: can ER predict the next trend? (my test)

  7. 7. One-line summary

From Perry Kaufman, Smarter Trading (1995); also in Murphy, Technical Analysis of the Financial Markets, Moving Averages, pdf p263 (see ../concepts/murphy_moving_averages.md §10). Numbers below measured on my own NSE data (Oct 2026). Education, not investment advice.

1. The problem it solves

A normal moving average has a fixed speed. A fast one (10-day) follows trends quickly but whipsaws in a range. A slow one (50-day) ignores the noise but enters trends late. KAMA changes its own speed bar by bar:

  • fast when price is moving cleanly in one direction;
  • almost frozen when price is going up and down without getting anywhere.

2. The Efficiency Ratio (ER) — "how straight was the road?"

  • ER = 1: every bar moved the same way, a perfectly straight trend.
  • ER = 0: price walked a lot but ended where it started, pure chop.
  • Physics picture (../concepts/price_physics_basics.md): ER = displacement ÷ path length. It compares drift (direction) with noise.

Example, 10 days. The stock goes 100 → 110 in daily steps of +1. Net = 10, path = 10, so ER = 1.0. Another stock goes 100 → 102 → 99 → 103 → 100 → 104 → 101 → 103 → 100 → 102 → 101. Net = 1, path = 2+3+4+3+4+3+2+3+2+1 = 27, so ER = 0.04.

3. From ER to KAMA (Kaufman's default 10, 2, 30)

ERSCActs likeMeaning
1.00.444~3-day EMAtrend: hugs price
0.50.133~14-day EMAmixed
0.20.034~60-day EMAweak
0.00.004~500-day EMAchop: line goes flat

The square is the key trick: an ER of 0.2 does not give "20% of the fast speed". It gives about 8% of it, so in a range the line almost stops moving and price crosses it back and forth without dragging it.

Nifty in October 2026 (real): ER(10) was 0.58 on 8 Oct (SC 0.17, KAMA moving); since 13 Oct it has been 0.02–0.31, and KAMA has sat at 22,768–22,800 for two weeks while Nifty swung between 22,600 and 23,150. The flat line is the signal: sideways.

4. How do we tell trending vs sideways?

Read ER directly (the same number KAMA uses):

ER(10) on daily barsRead it asHow often on Nifty, 2009–2026
> 0.5trending26% of days
0.2 – 0.5mixed / weak trend41%
< 0.2sideways33%

Nifty's median daily ER(10) is 0.31, and a pure random walk scores 0.27. So most of the time, the market's "trendiness" over 10 days is close to what coin-flips would produce.

The threshold depends on n. The longer the window, the more noise the path adds, so ER falls. Nifty's median ER is 0.31 for n = 10, 0.21 for n = 20, 0.13 for n = 60 and 0.09 for n = 120. Never reuse a "0.3" threshold across different lengths or timeframes. Pick it from that market's own percentiles.

Other tools that answer the same question:

ToolTrend whenSideways when
ADX (14)> 25< 20
Choppiness Index (14)< 38> 62
MA slopethe 50-day MA rises or falls by > ~0.5 ATR over 10 barsflat
Bollinger Band widthexpandingsqueezed (often before a breakout)
Price vs 200-DMAfar above or belowcrossing it back and forth
KAMA itselfslopingflat

ER and the Choppiness Index are nearly the same idea (net move vs total path). ADX measures directional movement vs range. All of them describe the bars you already have. Which one to use for what, tested on 185 Nifty 200 stocks: trend_vs_sideways_tools.md.

5. The important part: can ER predict the next trend? (my test)

I asked: if today's ER is high, will the next 10 days also trend? (Nifty daily 2009–2026, plus 188 Nifty 200 stocks.)

ER(10) todayMedian ER of the next 10 daysP(next 10 days trend, ER > 0.4)
0 – 0.2 (sideways)0.3138%
0.2 – 0.40.3340%
0.4 – 0.60.3039%
0.6 – 1.0 (strong trend)0.2934%
  • Correlation between today's ER and the next period's ER: −0.04 (10-day), −0.11 (20-day), −0.04 (60-day) on Nifty. The median across 188 stocks is −0.03. A random walk gives −0.02. Hourly Nifty bars give −0.01.
  • In contrast, volatility does persist: the correlation of 10-day volatility with the next 10 days' is +0.58.

So: ER tells you what the market is doing, not what it will do. A sideways stretch is as likely to be followed by a trend as by more chop. "How much it moves" is predictable; "whether it moves in a straight line" is not, at least not from ER.

That is why KAMA is useful as an adaptive tool, not as a forecaster:

  • It needs no prediction. It reacts to whatever ER the market gives it, bar by bar, and stays quiet in chop.
  • The cost: when a trend begins after a range, ER starts low, so KAMA is slow at the start of the move. It catches the middle of the trend, like every moving average.
  • A crossover on a flat KAMA still happens in a range. Kaufman adds a filter: only act when KAMA has moved by more than a fraction (e.g. 0.1–0.2) of the standard deviation of its recent changes.

6. How to use it (and what my backtests say)

  1. As a regime filter: skip trend signals (MA cross, breakout, MACD) when ER or ADX says "sideways", and skip mean-reversion signals when it says "trending". It removes some whipsaws; it does not make a losing signal profitable.
    • My Adaptive SuperTrend test (../../../projects/trading experiments/supertrend_di_backtest.py, er_len=14, er_thr=0.30) used exactly this filter. It still lost to costs on short timeframes.
    • The filter that helped most in my tests was the slow one: Nifty above its 200-DMA (+0.26 Sharpe, see ../backtests/backtest_results_summary.md). Slow filters work because they describe the big trend, which lasts longer.
  2. As a trailing exit: KAMA flattens in pauses and speeds up in strong moves, so it suits trailing a position.
  3. Use daily or weekly bars. On 15-min or 1-hour bars, ER flips between "trend" and "chop" many times a day, and every flip costs charges (../concepts/breakeven_move_fyers.md).
  4. Not yet tested by me: a full KAMA crossover / KAMA-filter backtest on Nifty 200 daily. Worth a project if I want the number.

7. One-line summary

ER = net move ÷ total path. High means trending, low means sideways. KAMA uses ER² to pick its speed. ER describes the present well, but on Nifty it has zero power to forecast whether the next 10–60 days will trend. Use it to adapt, not to predict.
